newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam's hometown holds huge birthday parade.
newsitem.headline: Saddam's hometown holds huge birthday parade.

text.p: Tens of thousands of Iraqis staged a huge parade on Monday in President Saddam Hussein's home town, marking his 60th birthday with pledges to stay loyal to him forever.

The crowd who came from various towns walked past the reviewing stand at a parade ground on the outskirts of Tikrit, 170 km (105 miles) north of Baghdad, shouting "With our blood, with our soul, we shall defend you, Saddam!"
The display of loyalty was one of many held across the country except for Kurdish areas, which have been outside Saddam's control since the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.

The parade was attended by almost all Iraqi leaders except Saddam, who remains firmly entrenched in power despite the ruinous war and punitive trade sanctions imposed by the United Nations for Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
Izzat Ibrahim, Vice-President of the Revolutionary Command Council, presided over the ceremonies in Tikrit which in recent years have been turned into one of Iraq's national festivals.
Young girls wearing Arab and Kurdish costumes were brought forward to dance and sing a birthday song: "Happy birthday to you, Saddam, you are the beloved of millions."
Groups of military men paraded in front of Ibrahim while formations of air force planes and helicopter gunships flew over the agricultural town. The celebrations lasted for two hours.
Foreign reporters were allowed to attend under escort by Information Ministry officials.
Women, students, tribesmen and chieftains carrying banners in praise of Saddam swirled to the strains of folk music as they passed the reviewing stand where the leaders were watching.
Farmers and tribesmen who travelled to Tikrit from the rest of the country pitched tents along the streets and the highway to Baghdad, offering free coffee and food.
Many men and women carrying Iraqi flags were seen along the highway walking or riding horses on their way to Baghdad to display their loyalty.
Iraqi radio and television aired special programmes and during the breaks, a choir of young girls and boys sang: "Happy birthday to you, Papa Saddam."
Shabab television, run by Saddam's eldest son Uday who escaped an assassination attempt last December, changed its name to "Birthday TV" and ran special programmes to mark the occasion.
